zh:
后来，最不喜欢背书的小萝卜，将师兄师姐们的研究一字一字、仔仔细细地记了下来。他找到了不见山，又启程出山游学。或许是要去往各派，学许多新的知识；或许会在某天突然归来，潜心墨门学问，来日好挣得那“鹤”的授号。
后来，丁苹把邵伋的手稿带回了不见山。他的研究在山中真派上了大用场，许多人问是哪位天才的想法，她便大声地告诉他们他的名字。再后来，她出不见山，去了江南，去了蜀地，去了荆楚，去了大漠……她把那些日子写进书里，给很多很多人看。等将来与故友团圆了，她也可以做讲的那一个了。
后来，符晓各处搜罗书籍，办了个看书不收钱的书馆，机关的、算学的、诗文的、传奇故事的……应有尽有。她规划事情，还是如往日那样井井有条，要让想看书的都能看到。只是蝴蝶落到书上的时候，思绪会乱。她会想起一个人，那个爱看书的极温柔的人。
后来，提前护送乡邻南下的李昉去朝中当了官，位至宰相，恪尽职守。他又经历了许多大风大浪，但忘不掉的，仍旧是那一方小小的书院。书院重建，那些人却再也回不来了。微风吹过，帮他拂开书页的时候，他又觉得他们好像始终都在。
后来……还有许许多多的后来。
en:
Later, Little Radish, who once hated memorizing texts above all, recorded his seniors' research word for word with absolute care. He found Hidden Mountain and set out to travel and study. Perhaps he would visit various sects to learn new skills; perhaps he would return one day to master the Mohist teachings and earn the title of "Crane."
Later, Ding Ping brought Shao Ji's manuscripts back to Hidden Mountain. His research proved invaluable there; when people asked whose brilliant mind conceived it, she proudly declared his name. Later, she left Hidden Mountain for Jiangnan, Shu, Jingchu, and the great deserts, writing of those journeys for all to read. When she finally reunited with old friends, she would be the one telling the stories.
Later, Fu Xiao gathered books from all corners and opened a free library, stocking everything from mechanics and mathematics to poetry and folk tales. She organized it with her usual meticulous order, ensuring anyone who wished to read could do so. Yet, whenever a butterfly landed on a page, her thoughts would drift back to a gentle soul who loved to read.
Later, Li Fang, who had escorted the villagers south, became a court official and rose to Chancellor, serving with absolute devotion. He weathered many storms, yet he could never forget that small academy. The academy was rebuilt, but those people could never return. Yet when the breeze rustled the pages of his books, he felt as if they were still there.
Later... there were many more laters.

两年前的鼓声也有血的味道，那时她还是龙蛟帮的大小姐。洪水滔天她找不到爹娘，瓠子堤破她找不到阿错，后来他们真的走了。冯如之站在黄河边，波涛没过她的脚踝，她对着手足无措的众人说，从今往后，我来当这个堂主。

en:
When the drumbeats sounded, Feng Ruzhi smelled blood, her own blood. Behind the Nuo mask, she swallowed the blood, stood up, and reached for the flying silk ball. The silk ball reflected in her eyes, and amidst the bright red, she heard the drumbeat from two years ago again. 
The drumbeat two years ago also smelled of blood. Back then, she was still the young lady of the Dragon Hall. When the flood raged, she couldn't find her parents. When the Huzhi Dyke broke, she couldn't find A-Cuo. Later, they really left her. Feng Ruzhi stood by the Yellow River, waves lapping at her ankles, and said to the helpless crowd, "From now on, I will be the hall master." 
The silk ball drew closer to her.

zh:
封龙山者，北岳之英援，三条之别神。相传夏禹治水时，曾封蛟龙于此山，故而得名。 
千年以来，封龙山常享典礼祭祀，又得碑颂相记，香火绵续不绝。汉时学者李躬于此传道授业，是为封龙书院之前身；唐代名士郭震入山得剑，作《宝剑诗》而结庐讲学。至此，山中文脉兴盛，学子倾心。
时值四时失序，幽云裂土。有墨门长老鹤心怀大义，履险蹈危，兴建封龙书院。举有教无类之旗，不问出身、不分贵贱，春风化雨，泽被天下。虽乱世非一日能平，然余所见处，薪火相传，火种不熄也。
en:
A majestic crest of the Northern Peak, Dragonbend Mountain rises where three great mountain ranges meet. Legend tells that when Yu the Great tamed the ancient floods, he imprisoned a mighty flood-dragon beneath these very crags, forever giving the mountain its name.
For centuries, Dragonbend Mountain has stood as a revered sanctuary. The smoke of temple incense has never faded, and countless stone steles remain to sing its praises. It was here, during the Han Dynasty, that the scholar Li Gong first gathered his students, laying the foundation for what would become the Dragonbend Academy. Ages later, the illustrious Tang Dynasty scholar Guo Zhen ventured into these woods, unearthed a legendary blade, and wrote his renowned Ode to the Precious Sword. He built a humble retreat to teach, and from then on, a rich scholarly tradition flourished, drawing eager minds from across the realm.
Yet it was during a dark era of endless war and fractured empires that the Mohist Elder Crane took his boldest stand. Driven by a profound sense of duty, he braved the perils of a broken world to officially establish the Dragonbend Academy. Under the banner of education for all, he welcomed every seeker of knowledge regardless of birth or blood, hoping to heal a wounded realm through the grace of learning. Though a chaotic age cannot be quieted in a single day, one truth endures: the torch of wisdom has passed from generation to generation, and the ember of the human spirit has never died.

栾城之名，溯自春秋晋帅栾书。至后晋，燕云既失，此地累遭战火威胁。田园荒芜，生计无着。民不甘坐以待毙，遂另辟蹊径，赴封龙书院习织，归后融旧贯新，凭慧心巧手，竟于乱世中织出“栾城土布”之盛名。此后，城中家家户户皆以织布为业，以悬挂彩布为荣。彼时入城，机杼声不绝于耳，千家悬彩，灿若落霞。
惜乎！“昔日千家悬彩布，今朝城头换敌旗。”如今机声已寂，彩布尽失，唯余虏旗招摇。风过处，依稀可见几抹殷红仍悬于木架之上，恍惚间，似能听见满城呜咽，萦绕不散。
en:
This hall is the heart of Luancheng County, a land that turned to the loom for survival when war left its fields fallow. The famed "Luancheng Homespun" brought prosperity, and the county once rang with shuttles, its eaves bright with cloth.
Now, the looms are silent. Invaders' flags replace the vibrant banners, leaving only crimson stains on empty frames to echo the county's sob.

zh:
【文王世子第八】

文王之为世子，朝于王季，日三。鸡初鸣而衣服，至于寝门外，问内竖之御者曰：“今日安否何如？”内竖曰：“安。”文王乃喜。及日中，又至，亦如之。及莫，又至，亦如之。其有不安节，则内竖以告文王，文王色忧，行不能正履。王季腹膳，然后亦复初。食上，必在，视寒暖之节，食下，问所膳；命膳宰曰：“末有原！”应曰：“诺。”然后退。武王帅而行之，不敢有加焉。文王有疾，武王不脱冠带而养。文王一饭，亦一饭；文王再饭，亦再饭。旬有二日乃间。文王谓武王曰：“女何梦矣？”武王对曰：“梦帝与我九龄。”文王曰：“女以为何也？”武王曰：“西方有九国焉，君王其终抚诸？”文王曰：“非也。古者谓年龄，齿亦龄也。我百尔九十，吾与尔三焉。”文王九十七乃终，武王九十三而终。成王幼，不能莅阼，周公相，践阼而治。抗世子法于伯禽，欲令成王之知父子、君臣、长幼之道也；成王有过，则挞伯禽，所以示成王世子之道也。文王之为世子也。
凡学世子及学士，必时。春夏学干戈，秋冬学羽籥，皆于东序。小乐正学干，大胥赞之。龠师学戈，龠师丞赞之。胥鼓南。春诵夏弦，大师诏之。瞽宗秋学礼，执礼者诏之；冬读书，典书者诏之。礼在瞽宗，书在上庠。凡祭与养老乞言，合语之礼，皆小乐正诏之于东序。大乐正学舞干戚，语说，命乞言，皆大乐正授数，大司成论说在东序。
凡侍坐于大司成者，远近间三席，可以问。终则负墙，列事未尽，不问。凡学，春官释奠于其先师，秋冬亦如之。凡始立学者，必释奠于先圣先师；及行事，必以币。凡释奠者，必有合也，有国故则否。凡大合乐，必遂养老。凡语于郊者，必取贤敛才焉。或以德进，或以事举，或以言扬。曲艺皆誓之，以待又语。三而一有焉，乃进其等，以其序，谓之郊人，远之。于成均以及取爵于上尊也。始立学者，既兴器用币，然后释菜不舞不授器，乃退。傧于东序，一献，无介语可也。教世子。
……
en:
【The King Wen as Heir Apparent, Chapter VIII】

When King Wen was heir apparent, he paid court to King Ji three times a day. At the first crow of the rooster, he would dress and go to the gate of the bedchamber, asking the attending inner attendant, "How is the peace and well-being today?" The attendant would reply, "All is well." Then King Wen would be pleased. At midday, he would come again, and do the same. At dusk, he would come again, and do the same. If there was any discomfort, the attendant would inform King Wen, and his countenance would show concern, and he could not walk with steady steps. When King Ji's meals were served, he would always be present, checking the temperature and warmth; when the meal was removed, he would ask what had been eaten, and order the steward of meals, saying, "Do not bring back any leftover!" The steward would reply, "Yes." Then he would withdraw. King Wu followed this example and did not dare to exceed it. When King Wen fell ill, King Wu did not remove his cap and belt while attending to him. If King Wen ate one meal, he would eat one meal; if King Wen ate two, he would eat two. After twelve days, King Wen recovered. King Wen said to King Wu, "What dream did you have?" King Wu replied, "I dreamed that God gave me nine spans of life." King Wen said, "What do you think of this?" King Wu said, "In the west there are nine states; perhaps you, my lord, will ultimately pacify them?" King Wen said, "No. In ancient times, age was called 'years,' and teeth also signified age. I am a hundred, and you are ninety; I will give you three of mine." King Wen died at ninety-seven, and King Wu died at ninety-three. King Cheng was young and could not ascend to the throne, so the Duke of Zhou acted as regent, stepping up to the throne to govern. He set up the model of the heir apparent before Bo Qin, wishing to make King Cheng understand the ways of father and son, ruler and minister, and elder and younger. When King Cheng erred, he would flog Bo Qin, thereby showing King Cheng the way of the heir apparent. Such was King Wen's conduct as heir apparent.
In all instruction of the heir apparent and scholars, there must be proper seasons. In spring and summer, they learned the use of shield and spear; in autumn and winter, the feather and flute—all in the Eastern Hall. The Lesser Music Director taught the shield, and the Grand Assistant aided him. The Flute Master taught the spear, and the Flute Master's Deputy aided him. The Assistant beat time for the southern airs. In spring they recited, in summer they strummed, and the Grand Music Master instructed them. In autumn, rites were learned in the Blind Musicians' Hall, with the keeper of rites instructing; in winter, documents were studied, with the keeper of records instructing. Rites were in the Blind Musicians' Hall, and documents in the Upper Hall. For all sacrifices, the nourishing of the aged, the seeking of counsel, and the rites of joint discourse, the Lesser Music Director instructed them in the Eastern Hall. The Grand Music Director taught the dance with shield and axe, the explanations of discourse, and the commands for seeking counsel—all these the Grand Music Director assigned in number, and the Grand Minister of Studies expounded in the Eastern Hall.
Whenever one sat in attendance on the Grand Minister of Studies, the distance between them was three mats, so that questions could be asked. When finished, one would turn to the wall; if the matters being discussed were not yet complete, one did not ask. In all studies, in spring the officers offered libations to their former teachers, and in autumn and winter likewise. Whenever a school was first established, libations must be offered to the former sages and former teachers; and in performing these rites, silk must be used. For all libation ceremonies, there must be a gathering; but if there were national mourning, this was not done. Whenever there was a grand concert of music, the nourishing of the aged must follow. Whenever discourse was held in the suburbs, the worthy and talented must be selected and gathered. Some advanced through virtue, some were raised through affairs, some were praised through speech. Those with minor skills were all admonished, awaiting further discourse. If among three attempts one succeeded, they were advanced in rank, according to their order, and were called "suburban men," kept at a distance. At the completion of studies and the taking of the cup from the upper vessel, when a school was first established, after the instruments were set up and silk was used, then vegetables were offered without dancing and without giving instruments, and then they withdrew. They were entertained in the Eastern Hall with a single offering, without an intermediary or discourse. This was the instruction of the heir apparent.

“常衔西山之木石，以堙于东海。”
海仍无垠。
已死魂灵堕于深水，反觉日寒月暖，空煎人寿。
偶尔亦会有水声，有木虺撞击声，有机关活动声。该是哪个来探险的顽劣弟子，随便打发他出去吧。
不过有个小不点，似找到了关窍。一层一层，摸到了他的身边，来到了他的眼前。
真年轻啊。
墨山道何时来了个这样好的年轻后辈？让张万师想起师父鹤将两只瓷娃娃丢到他面前的那个下午。
不，不对……似乎不只是那个下午，还有满山红枫为他送行的那个清晨。
会好的……真的会好吗？
小家伙，你能填了那海吗？
要多少精卫，才能填了那海呢？
en:
"Forever she carries twigs and stones from the Western Hills, striving to fill the boundless Eastern Sea."
Yet the sea remains vast and unyielding.

A ghost cast into the depths, she finds the sun cold and the moon warm, the slow, hollow burning of a life that will not end.

Now and then he hears the lap of water, the heavy thrum of a wooden viper, the rhythmic click of turning gears.
Likely just some wayward disciple out for a lark.
Send them away, and be done with it.

Yet one young sprout has somehow found the way through. Layer by layer, they have worked their way in, until they are standing right there before him.

How young.

Since when did Mohist Hill produce a young soul like this? It takes him back to that afternoon when Master Crane sent two young ones to him.
No... not only then.
There was also that dawn when the mountains blazed red with maple, and these young principles came to see him off

Things will get better... will they, truly?

Little one, do you think you can fill that sea?
How many Jingwei would it take, to fill an endless sea like that?

zh:
话说这江湖上凡是读过话本子的， 恐怕鲜有几人未听过“太湖梨膏糖”的声名。“太湖梨膏糖”以其对江湖消息的了解，以及极佳的故事编排实力，创作出了包括《霸道狂侠：道主》、《吾愿做九流门小姐的狗》等话本名篇。然而自离恨天书社横空出世后，“太湖梨膏糖”的人气便日日下跌。为与离恨天书社争先，梨膏糖笔耕不辍，异常高产，也因此在字里行间渐渐暴露出其真实的身份……
经过江湖无数话本爱好者的明察暗访，太湖梨膏糖的身份终于浮出水面，这位擅长叙情的风流写手，竟是梨园天下行走，人称“冷面仙姑”的韩烟罗。消息一出，天下无不惊愕，可转念一想，太湖梨膏，不就是暗指梨园？想那梨园自创派以来，便一力用戏文演绎江湖故事，留下无数缠绵悱恻的故事名篇，可到了近些年，竟是产出寥寥，甚至被那离恨天夺了风头，作为园主亲传弟子，韩烟罗怎能不急。如此高产，恐怕也不过是为了证明“话本正统在梨园”，实在是可叹、可敬……
en:
In the jianghu, anyone who's read a storybook or two has surely heard of the name "Taihu Pear Syrup." Famous for their keen grasp of martial world gossip and masterful storytelling, Candy Lady created beloved works like Tyrannical Warrior: Dao Lord and I'd Gladly Be a Hound for the Lady of Nine Mortal Ways. Yet ever since the sudden rise of Lament Scriptorium, Candy Lady's popularity has been in decline every day. To compete with Lamentation Heavens, Candy Lady picked up the pace and churned out tale after tale. Only to unwittingly reveal clues to their true identity between the lines.

After countless secret investigations conducted by devoted storybook fans, the truth finally came to light: the romantic wordsmith behind Candy Lady was none other than Han Yanluo, the famed "Ice-Faced Fairy" of the Masked Troupe. The news stunned the jianghu. Then again, in hindsight, "Candy Lady," "Masked Troupe", the hints were there all along. Since its founding, the Masked Troupe had been devoted to dramatizing the legends of the martial world, crafting countless poignant classics. Yet in recent years, their output dwindled, overshadowed by the Lamentation Heavens. As a direct disciple of the Masked Troupe's master, how could Han Yanluo not be anxious? Her feverish writing was likely her way of proving that Masked Troupe is still the king of all storybooks, an effort both lamentable and admirable.

zh: “尔”者近也，“雅”者正也，乃训诂之渊海、六艺之钤键。观《隋书·经籍志》，此书尝附于《孝经》之列，盖以其正名辨物，有裨于经学之始。今人多视之为读经之阶梯，通古之舟楫，其以“初、哉、首、基”同训为“始”，正乃一字见心，万象归宗，为天下读书人解千古之惑也。
en: "Er" signifies nearness; "ya" signifies correctness. Together they form a vast sea of classical exegesis and a master key to the Six Arts. As recorded in the Book of Sui: Treatise on Classics, this work was once placed alongside "The Classic of Filial Piety," for its role in rectifying names and distinguishing things made it a fitting companion to the study of the classics. Scholars today regard it as the first rung on the ladder of classical learning and the vessel by which one crosses into antiquity. That it glosses "chu," "zai," "shou," and "ji" all under the single meaning of "beginning" is itself a testament to how one word may reveal the heart of a matter, drawing ten thousand things back to a single source, resolving for readers across all ages the great riddles left by the ancients.

zh:
以杜辰非的身手之高，要杀一百个虏人并非难事，也用不着多少时间。然而或许是曾经中箭的教训，又或许是有约在身，他一改过去那不要命的打法，而是变得谨小慎微起来。
如此几年，杜辰非终是完成了杀一百虏人的约定，他把自己杀人的刀拿到铁匠铺，重打了一把剔骨切肉的菜刀。
再进镇戍仓，他左寻右探，始终不见老人的身影。正当他疑惑时，忽然听到有人轻轻喊了他的名字，像是在确认什么一般。他转过身，见到一个年轻人的面孔，眉宇里和老人有些相似。
年轻人是老张头的儿子，老张头前不久摔了一跤，再也没能起来。弥留之际，还在念叨着有个杜大侠要来继承他的肉摊，让小张在这里等着。其实他一点也不信杜辰非真的会回来，只是为着父亲的遗愿，只好多等上一等。
杜辰非有些好奇，既然老张头有孩子，何必要把铺子留给他这个外人。
小张笑了笑，说他一点儿也不想继承肉摊，困在这里一辈子，多没意思。这几年他天天听老张头讲，杜大侠在外头，要杀一百个虏人才回来，这般豪情与气魄，才是他想要过的人生。说罢，他进屋翻出了一个箱子，告诉杜辰非这便是五味脯的秘方。
年轻人系好腰间的钢刀，翻身策马潇洒离去。
杜辰非握住手里的菜刀，重新摆起老张肉铺。
边关战火一日更甚一日，镇戍仓内驻扎的将士换了一批又一批，所幸小张隔些时候便能回来一趟，说自己又杀了几个虏人，救了多少百姓。还说等他杀满一百个虏人，准比当年的杜大侠还要快。最近一次回来时，他和老杜说要上中渡桥去，那里聚集了不少虏人，准能杀个痛快。
等这趟回来，说什么也得让他亲手做一次五味脯，杜辰非心里想。
en:
Given Du Chenfei's superb martial skills, slaying a hundred foreign invaders was hardly a difficult task, nor would it take much time. Yet, perhaps due to the lesson learned from the arrow wound, or perhaps because he was bound by a promise, he abandoned his former death-defying fighting style and became cautious and prudent.
Thus, after several years, Du Chenfei finally fulfilled the pact of killing a hundred invaders. He took his killing blade to the blacksmith and had it reforged into a cleaver for deboning and slicing meat.
Entering the Toilgrain Barn once more, he searched high and low, but could not find the old man anywhere.
Just as he was feeling puzzled, he suddenly heard someone softly call his name, as if confirming something.
He turned around and saw the face of a young man, whose features bore some resemblance to the old man.
The young man was Old Man Zhang's son. Not long ago, Old Man Zhang had taken a fall and was never able to get back up. On his deathbed, he kept muttering that Hero Du would come to inherit his meat stall, and told his son to wait for him here. In truth, he didn't believe for a second that Du Chenfei would actually return, but for the sake of his father's dying wish, he had no choice but to wait a little longer.
Du Chenfei was somewhat curious: since Old Man Zhang had a son, why did he insist on leaving the stall to an outsider like him?
Zhang smiled, saying he had no desire whatsoever to inherit the meat stall; being trapped here for a lifetime would be too boring. Over the past few years, he had listened to Old Man Zhang tell the story every day of how Hero Du was out there and would only return after killing a hundred foreign invaders. Such heroism and spirit were exactly the life he wanted to live. With that said, he dug out a chest and told Du Chenfei that this was the secret recipe for the Five Flavor Jerky.
The young man fastened the steel broadsword at his waist, leaped onto his horse, and rode away with dashing swagger.
Du Chenfei gripped the kitchen cleaver in his hand and reopened Old Man Zhang's meat stall.
The flames of war at the border grew fiercer by the day, and the troops stationed in the Toilgrain Barn were rotated batch after batch. Fortunately, Zhang would return every so often, recounting how many more invaders he had slain and how many commoners he had saved. He also boasted that when he reached his quota of a hundred invaders, it would surely be faster than Hero Du back in the day. During his most recent return, he told Du that he was heading to Zhongdu Bridge; a large number of invaders were gathering there, and he would surely be able to kill to his heart's content.
When he returns from this trip, I must make him prepare the Five Flavor Jerky with his own hands, no matter what, Du Chenfei thought to himself.
RobinsEeker

Some of them I've already taken apart and put back together. Once I've studied them enough, I'll be able to make my own out of wood. Some are too complicated for me to copy, sure, but that just means they're rare, and rare things sell for more, right? Once I've built up enough stock, I'll make a trip to Qinghe and Kaifeng and sell the lot. Won't I make a killing?
Sure, my luck was rotten, and I got caught by some geezer, but thankfully,I have a good reputation, so everyone came to plead my case. I'm just running a small business, not doing anything immoral. People ought to be reasonable, right?

和家猪不同，山猪是莽林深谷的骄子。它们奔走于山峦间，或于泥淖中翻滚，或于林间闲步。古人谓之“豕突”，形容其奔走迅捷。但据不见山居民称，山猪亦有害怕之物，谓之马猴。
en:
The sow follows the piglets; she grunts and they squeal.

Unlike domestic pigs, boars are the pride of deep forests and valleys. They gallop across mountains, wallow in mud, or stroll through woods. The ancients called their charge "Su Tu" to describe their speed. Residents of Hidden Mountain say boars fear only one thing: the Macaque.

zh:
同门亲启：

俺说什么来着？这舞台逐艺，就跟战场一样，瞬息万变。
近来你的演出俺也看了，曲调婉转，舞姿曼妙，就一个字：绝！
可惜戏班整体热度未达，暂时降级，实为可惜。
戏班虽有遗憾，你的实力有目共睹，仍可留于原位继续精进。
花有重开日，人有再来时。复活赛已在筹备，此番暂别，不过是养精蓄锐。
来日必能见你重回舞台中央，一展所长。切莫气馁，静候佳音！
en:
To My Fellow Disciples, 

What did I say? This stage of art is like a battlefield, changing in the blink of an eye. 
I've watched your recent performances too. Graceful melodies and exquisite dance moves! 
It's a pity the Troupe's overall Popularity didn't meet the mark, resulting in a temporary demotion. Truly regrettable. 
Yet your strength is evident to all, and you can remain in your current position to continue refining your skills. 
Flowers may bloom again; people may have another chance. The revival match is coming soo. This temporary farewell is merely for gathering strength and resting. 
We will surely see you return to the center of the stage someday, showcasing your strengths. Don't be discouraged. Await good news!

zh:
鹳长老的新春寄语

小后学，前些时日在山中寻宝一事，你做得很好。这几日我与几位长老在墨城内走动，发觉弟子们已不再整日窝在书桌前，而是愿意到外头来做做操、跑跑步，如此甚好。学术研究与强身健体，二者皆不可荒废，才是我等长久钻研之道。
山中事务繁忙，老夫不能亲至开封，便在机关人身上捎上祝福。
今日，老夫就不来考考你了。毕竟，这新岁的考题，得自己出给自己，才是最合适的。
小后学，新岁快乐。望你百尺竿头，更进一步。若是有空，记得常回山门看看。
en:
Elder Stork's Spring Festival Greetings

Young learner, you did very well searching for treasures in the mountains a while ago. In recent days, as I have walked around Mohist City with several elders, I have noticed that the disciples no longer spend all day hunched over their desks, but are willing to go outside to do exercises and run around. This is very good. Both academic research and physical fitness are indispensable; this is the way for us to pursue long-term studies.
Affairs in the mountains are busy. I cannot personally visit Kaifeng, so I will send my blessings through the mechanical figure.
Today, I won't quiz you. After all, the test for the new year must be set by oneself to be most appropriate.
Young learner, happy new year. May you make further progress. If you have time, remember to return to the mountain to visit.

zh:
【尽心章句上】

孟子曰：尽其心者，知其性也。知其性，则知天也。存其心，养其性，所以事天也。夭寿不贰，修身以俟之，所以立命也。
孟子曰：莫非命也，顺受其正。是故知命者不立乎岩墙之下。尽其道而死者，正命也；桎梏死者，非正命也。
孟子曰：求则得之，舍则失之，是求有益于得也，求在我者也。求之有道，得之有命，是求无益于得也，求在外者也。
孟子曰：万物皆备于我矣。反身而诚，乐莫大焉。强恕而行，求仁莫近焉。
孟子曰：行之而不著焉，习矣而不察焉，终身由之而不知其道者，众也。
孟子曰：人不可以无耻，无耻之耻，无耻矣。
孟子曰：耻之于人大矣。为机变之巧者，无所用耻焉。不耻不若人，何若人有？
孟子曰：古之贤王好善而忘势。古之贤士何独不然？乐其道而忘人之势。故王公不致敬尽礼，则不得亟见之。见且由不得亟，而况得而臣之乎？
孟子谓宋句践曰：子好游乎？吾语子游。人知之亦嚣嚣，人不知亦嚣嚣。
曰：何如斯可以嚣嚣矣？
曰：尊德乐义，则可以嚣嚣矣。故士穷不失义，达不离道。穷不失义，故士得己焉；达不离道，故民不失望焉。古之人得志，泽加于民；不得志，修身见于世。穷则独善其身，达则兼善天下。
孟子曰：待文王而后兴者，凡民也。若夫豪杰之士，虽无文王犹兴。
孟子曰：附之以韩、魏之家，如其自视欿然，则过人远矣。
孟子曰：以佚道使民，虽劳不怨；以生道杀民，虽死不怨杀者。
孟子曰：霸者之民，𬴐虞如也；王者之民，皞皞如也。杀之而不怨，利之而不庸，民日迁善而不知为之者。夫君子所过者化，所存者神，上下与天地同流，岂曰小补之哉？
孟子曰：仁言不如仁声之入人深也，善政不如善教之得民也。善政民畏之，善教民爱之。善政得民财，善教得民心。
孟子曰：人之所不学而能者，其良能也，所不虑而知者，其良知也。孩提之童，无不知爱其亲者，及其长也，无不知敬其兄也。亲亲，仁也；敬长，义也。无他，达之天下也。
孟子曰：舜之居深山之中，与木石居，与鹿豕游，其所以异于深山之野人者几希。及其闻一善言，见一善行，若决江河，沛然莫之能御也。
孟子曰：无为其所不为，无欲其所不欲，如此而已矣。
孟子曰：人之有德慧术知者，恒存乎疢疾。独孤臣孽子，其操心也危，其虑患也深，故达。
孟子曰：有事君人者，事是君则为容悦者也；有安社稷臣者，以安社稷为悦者也；有天民者，达可行于天下而后行之者也；有大人者，正己而物正者也。
孟子曰：君子有三乐，而王天下不与存焉。父母俱存，兄弟无故，一乐也；仰不愧于天，俯不怍于人，二乐也；得天下英才而教育之，三乐也。君子有三乐，而王天下不与存焉。
孟子曰：广土众民，君子欲之，所乐不存焉。中天下而立，定四海之民，君子乐之，所性不存焉。君子所性，虽大行不加焉，虽穷居不损焉，分定故也。君子所性，仁、义、礼、智根于心，其生色也，睟然见于面，盎于背，施于四体，四体不言而喻。
孟子曰：伯夷辟纣，居北海之滨，闻文王作，兴曰：盍归乎来！吾闻西伯善养老者。太公辟纣，居东海之滨，闻文王作，兴曰：盍归乎来？吾闻西伯善养老者。天下有善养老，则仁人以为己归矣。五亩之宅，树墙下以桑，匹妇𧖟之，则老者足以衣帛矣。五母鸡，二母彘，无失其时，老者足以无失肉矣。百亩之田，匹夫耕之，八口之家足以无饥矣。所谓西伯善养老者，制其田里，教之树畜，导其妻子，使养其老。五十非帛不暖，七十非肉不饱。不暖不饱，谓之冻馁。文王之民无冻馁之老者，此之谓也。
孟子曰：易其田畴，薄其税敛，民可使富也。食之以时，用之以礼，财不可胜用也。民非水火不生活，昏暮叩人之门户，求水火，无弗与者，至足矣。圣人治天下，使有菽粟如水火。菽粟如水火，而民焉有不仁者乎？
孟子曰：孔子登东山而小鲁，登太山而小天下。故观于海者难为水，游于圣人之门者难为言。观水有术，必观其澜。日月有明，容光必照焉。流水之为物也，不盈科不行；君子之志于道也，不成章不达。
孟子曰：鸡鸣而起，孳孳为善者，舜之徒也。鸡鸣而起，孳孳为利者，跖之徒也。欲知舜与跖之分，无他，利与善之间也。
……
en:
Chapter of Exhausting the Mind, Part 1

Mencius said: He who has exhausted all his mental constitution knows his nature. Knowing his nature, he knows Heaven. To preserve one's mental constitution and nourish one's nature is the way to serve Heaven. Not to be in two minds about the length of one's life but to cultivate oneself and wait for one's destiny is the way to establish one's destiny.

Mencius said: There is nothing that is not destiny. One submits to its proper mandate. That is why he who understands destiny does not stand under a precipitous wall. To die after having done one's best is to meet one's proper destiny. To die in fetters is not to meet one's proper destiny.

Mencius said: If you seek, you will get it; if you let it go, you will lose it. In such a case, seeking is of help to getting, and the seeking is within yourself. If seeking is according to the proper way, and getting is according to destiny, then seeking is of no help to getting, and the seeking is outside yourself.

Mencius said: All things are complete in me. There is no greater joy than to examine oneself and be sincere. In striving to be benevolent, nothing is closer than to act with forbearance.

Mencius said: To act without understanding, to practice without examining, to follow all one's life without knowing the way—this is the common lot of the multitude.

Mencius said: A man must not be without shame. The shame of being without shame is shamelessness indeed.

Mencius said: The sense of shame is of great importance to a man. He who indulges in craftiness has no use for shame. If a man is not ashamed of being inferior to others, how can he ever become their equal?

Mencius said: The worthy kings of old loved goodness and forgot about power. How could the worthy scholars of old be otherwise? They delighted in their way and forgot about the power of others. Therefore, if kings and dukes did not show them the utmost respect and observe all the rules of propriety, they were not permitted to see them frequently. If they could not see them frequently, how much less could they employ them as ministers?

Mencius said to Song Goujian: "Do you like to travel? Let me tell you about traveling. If people understand you, be content; if people do not understand you, be content."

Song Goujian asked: "What must one do to be content?"

Mencius replied: "If you honor virtue and delight in righteousness, you can be content. Therefore, a scholar, when in straitened circumstances, does not lose his righteousness; when successful, he does not leave the path. Not losing his righteousness when in straitened circumstances, the scholar retains his self-respect. Not leaving the path when successful, he does not disappoint the people. When the men of old realized their ambitions, they bestowed benefits on the people. When they did not realize their ambitions, they cultivated their personal character and became known to the world. In obscurity, they perfected themselves; in prominence, they perfected the whole world."

Mencius said: Those who wait for King Wen to arise and then follow him are ordinary people. As for the outstanding scholars, even without King Wen, they would arise.

Mencius said: If you add to a man the wealth of the families of Han and Wei, and he still looks upon himself as lacking, then he is far superior to others.

Mencius said: If you employ the people in accordance with the way of ease, they will toil without complaint. If you put the people to death in accordance with the way of life, they will die without resentment towards the executioner.

Mencius said: The people of a hegemon are cheerful and contented; the people of a true king are expansive and joyful. They are put to death without resentment; they are benefited without feeling indebted. The people daily move towards goodness without knowing who makes them do so. Where the gentleman passes, transformation occurs; where he abides, his influence is spiritual. He is in harmony with Heaven and Earth above and below. How can this be said to be a small contribution?

Mencius said: Kindly words do not enter so deep as a reputation for kindness. Good government does not win the people as does good education. Good government makes the people afraid; good education makes the people love. Good government wins the people's wealth; good education wins the people's hearts.

Mencius said: That which a man is capable of without having learned it is his innate ability. That which he knows without having to reflect upon it is his innate knowledge. There is no child who does not know to love his parents. When he grows up, there is no one who does not know to respect his elder brother. To love one's parents is benevolence; to respect one's elders is righteousness. There is nothing else but to extend these to the whole world.

Mencius said: When Shun lived in the depths of the mountains, dwelling among the trees and rocks, wandering with the deer and pigs, the difference between him and the rude rustics of the deep mountains was very slight. But when he heard one good word, saw one good deed, it was like a river breaking its banks, torrential and irresistible.

Mencius said: Do not do what you should not do; do not desire what you should not desire. That is all.

Mencius said: Men who possess virtue, wisdom, skill, and knowledge are often those who have suffered distress and calamity. It is only the solitary minister or the concubine's son who keep a constant anxiety, whose thoughts of troubles are deep, and therefore they attain understanding.

Mencius said: There are those who serve a prince—they serve whatever prince they can and seek to please him. There are those who are ministers that stabilize the state—they take pleasure in stabilizing the state. There are those who are Heaven's people—they act only when their principles can be practiced throughout the world. There are those who are great men—they rectify themselves and then all things are rectified.

Mencius said: The gentleman has three joys, and to be king over the world is not one of them. That his parents are both alive and his brothers are well—this is the first joy. That he can look up to Heaven without shame and look down upon men without embarrassment—this is the second joy. That he obtains the finest talents in the world and educates them—this is the third joy. The gentleman has three joys, and to be king over the world is not one of them.

Mencius said: Vast territory and a numerous population are what the gentleman desires, but his joy does not lie therein. To stand in the center of the world and bring peace to the people within the four seas—the gentleman delights in this, but his true nature does not lie therein. The true nature of the gentleman is such that it is not increased by great success nor diminished by living in obscurity, because it is fixed by his allotment. The true nature of the gentleman is benevolence, righteousness, propriety, and wisdom rooted in his heart. It manifests itself in his countenance, giving a sleek appearance to his face and a fullness to his back, and extends to his four limbs. The four limbs, without words, make it understood.

Mencius said: Bo Yi fled from Zhou and dwelt on the shore of the Northern Sea. Hearing that King Wen had arisen, he said with joy, "Why should I not return? I have heard that the Lord of the West is good at caring for the aged." Tai Gong fled from Zhou and dwelt on the shore of the Eastern Sea. Hearing that King Wen had arisen, he said with joy, "Why should I not return? I have heard that the Lord of the West is good at caring for the aged." If there is one in the world who is good at caring for the aged, then benevolent men regard him as their destination. With a homestead of five mu, planting mulberry trees around the walls, a woman can rear silkworms, and then the aged will have enough silk for clothing. With five hens and two sows, not missing their breeding seasons, the aged will have enough meat. With a hundred mu of fields, cultivated by a man, a family of eight can have enough to avoid hunger. What is meant by saying the Lord of the West was good at caring for the aged? He regulated their fields and dwellings, taught them to plant trees and rear animals, guided their wives and children to support their aged. At fifty, one cannot be warm without silk; at seventy, one cannot be full without meat. Not being warm and not being full is called suffering from cold and hunger. Among the people of King Wen, there were no aged who suffered from cold and hunger. This is what is meant.

Mencius said: Make the fields easy to cultivate, lighten the taxes and levies, and the people can be made wealthy. Let them eat according to the seasons, use according to propriety, and wealth will be more than enough. The people cannot live without water and fire. If at dusk one knocks on another's door seeking water or fire, there is none who will not give it, because these are in abundance. When a sage governs the world, he makes grain as abundant as water and fire. When grain is as abundant as water and fire, how can the people be other than benevolent?

Mencius said: Confucius ascended the Eastern Mountain, and the state of Lu appeared small. He ascended Mount Tai, and the whole world appeared small. Therefore, one who has observed the sea finds it difficult to be impressed by other waters. One who has studied under the gate of a sage finds it difficult to be impressed by other words. There is an art in observing water: one must observe its waves. The sun and moon have their brilliance; even a tiny crevice is illuminated. Water as a thing does not proceed without filling the hollows. The gentleman who is devoted to the Way does not advance without achieving clear accomplishment.

Mencius said: He who rises at cockcrow and diligently strives to do good is a follower of Shun. He who rises at cockcrow and diligently strives for profit is a follower of Zhi. To know the difference between Shun and Zhi, there is no other: it lies in the gap between profit and goodness.

zh:
棉花由印度传入我国，从中亚传入新疆的为西道棉，称为“白叠”。
但西道棉的传播在唐五代时主要局限于西域地区，止于河西。
当时新疆地区生产棉花的文物和例证，现藏于中国国家博物馆。
en:
Cotton first arrived in China from India. The variety that came through Central Asia into Xinjiang was called "Western Route Cotton," or "baidie." 
Yet during the Tang and Five Dynasties, its spread was limited to the Western Regions, stopping short at Hexi. 
Artifacts and records of Xinjiang's early cotton cultivation are now preserved in the National Museum of China.

长安大雪，二人梅下合奏，引一箫客踏雪驻足，未交一言持箫相和，知音相逢，尽在曲中。
三人共谱岁寒之曲，写松竹梅之格。松竹皆已成调，唯余梅曲未竟，止为残篇，殊为憾事。
而今乐者已渺，唯余残音袅袅。
en:
Once, a pair of blind musician siblings understood the world through melody, mastering the art of combat with music. It was said that when they played, plum blossoms shed snow and hidden fragrance wafted, like snow touched by notes. Thus, they were called the "Snowplum Requiem."
During a heavy snow in Chang'an, the two played beneath a plum tree. A flutist stopped in the snow, joined without a word, and harmony spoke what words could not.
The three composed a tune capturing the spirit of pine, bamboo, and plum. Pine and bamboo were set to tune, but the plum melody remained unfinished, a lasting regret.
Now the musicians are gone, leaving only faint echoes of a lingering sound.

zh:
告身书送到家里的时候，阿娘做的糍粑刚出锅。知县带着邻里前来祝贺，众人敲锣打鼓，欢喜非常。
洪钰看着眼前熙熙攘攘的人群有些发懵。直到那盖着朱印的告身书放在自己的手中，他才发觉，命运的重量早已千钧。
“悬泉驿，这是哪儿啊？”“哎，管是哪儿呢，洪家这小子可算是出息了！当大官儿了！”“以后可别忘了爷娘，你阿爷阿娘养你可不容易咧！”
七嘴八舌，都是乡亲们热烈而质朴的盼望。而洪钰却发现，爷娘的笑意里多了几分不舍。

几日后，月明星稀，寒鸦初醒。洪钰背着行囊走出村口的小路。最后一次，他回身遥望沉睡的村庄，重重地磕下三个头。
“钰一拜，拜谢爷娘，茹苦半生，护钰平安无忧。愿他日衣锦还乡，再伏膝前。”
“钰再拜，拜谢皇恩，委以重任，得以此身报国。愿有日建功立业，青史留名。”
“钰三拜……”洪钰顿了顿，“拜谢上苍，降此鸿运……愿此去平安顺遂，心想事达。”
“驿者，音书之所系，行李之所达。愿以双足布履，涉千里之山水，传万年之平安……”
彼时的他并不知道，这三拜如同谶语，宣告了他的命运——世事无常，他一步一步走向了相反的结局。
en:
When the official appointment document arrived at his home, the glutinous rice cakes made by his mother had just come out of the pot. The county magistrate came to congratulate him with neighbors, and everyone was overjoyed, beating gongs and drums. 
Hong Yu stared blankly at the bustling crowd. It wasn't until the official document sealed with a red stamp was placed in his hand that he felt the overwhelming weight of fate. 
"Celestial Spring Station, where's that?" "Ah, who cares where it is! The Hong family lad is finally making it big! Becoming a high official!" "Don't forget your parents later. It wasn't easy for them to raise you!" 
Voices chattered, warm, simple hopes from the villagers. Yet Hong Yu noticed a hint of reluctance in his parents' smiles. 

A few days later, under a bright moon and sparse stars, as jackdaws began to stir, Hong Yu walked out of the village path with his luggage on his back. For the last time, he turned to look at the sleeping village and kowtowed three times heavily. 
"Yu's first bow, in gratitude to Father and Mother, who endured hardship for half a lifetime, protecting Yu in peace and without worry. May the day come when I return in silken robes, to bow again at your knees." 
"Yu's second bow, in gratitude for imperial grace, entrusting me with heavy responsibility, allowing this body to serve the country. May a day come when I achieve merit and leave a name in the annals." 
"Yu's third bow..." Hong Yu paused, "...in gratitude to Heaven, for bestowing this great fortune... May this journey be safe and smooth, with wishes fulfilled and goals reached." 
"A relay station is where messages are linked, where travelers arrive. May I traverse thousands of miles of mountains and rivers with my feet and cloth shoes, carrying peace for ten thousand years…" 
At that time, he did not know that these three bows were like a prophecy, declaring his fate, the world's affairs are fickle, and step by step, she walked toward the opposite end.

zh:
【尧曰第二十】

尧曰：“咨！尔舜，天之历数在尔躬，允执其中。四海困穷，天禄永终。”舜亦以命禹。曰：“予小子履，敢用玄牡，敢昭告于皇皇后帝：有罪不敢赦，帝臣不蔽，简在帝心。朕躬有罪，无以万方；万方有罪，罪在朕躬。”周有大赉，善人是富。“虽有周亲，不如仁人。百姓有过，在予一人。”谨权量，审法度，修废官，四方之政行焉。兴灭国，继绝世，举逸民，天下之民归心焉。所重：民、食、丧、祭。宽则得众，信则民任焉，敏则有功，公则说。
子张问于孔子曰：“何如斯可以从政矣？”子曰：“尊五美，屏四恶，斯可以从政矣。”子张曰：“何谓五美？”子曰：“君子惠而不费，劳而不怨，欲而不贪，泰而不骄，威而不猛。”子张曰：“何谓惠而不费？”子曰：“因民之所利而利之，斯不亦惠而不费乎？择可劳而劳之，又谁怨？欲仁而得仁，又焉贪？君子无众寡，无小大，无敢慢，斯不亦泰而不骄乎？君子正其衣冠，尊其瞻视，俨然人望而畏之，斯不亦威而不猛乎？”子张曰：“何谓四恶？”子曰：“不教而杀谓之虐；不戒视成谓之暴；慢令致期谓之贼；犹之与人也，出纳之吝，谓之有司。”
孔子曰：“不知命，无以为君子也；不知礼，无以立也；不知言，无以知人也。”
en:
【Yao Said, Chapter 20】

Yao said, "Oh! You, Shun, the heavenly mandate now rests upon your person. Hold fast to the Mean. If within the four seas there is distress and poverty, your heavenly revenue will come to a perpetual end." Shun also used these words in giving charge to Yu. He said, "I, your little son, Li, venture to sacrifice a black bull, and make this clear declaration before the Sovereign Lord of Heaven: The guilty one I dare not pardon. The ministers of the Lord, I do not keep hidden. The examination is in the Lord's mind. If I commit any offense, it is not to be attributed to the myriad regions. But if in the myriad regions there is offense, the offense rests with me." Zhou had great gifts, and the good were enriched. "Although he has his near relatives, they are not equal to my virtuous men. If the people have any faults, let them fall on me alone." He carefully attended to the weights and measures, examined the body of the laws, restored the discarded offices, and the government of the four quarters was carried on. He revived states that had been extinguished, restored families whose line of succession had been broken, and called to office those who had retired into obscurity, so that all the people under heaven gave their hearts to him. What he valued were the people, food, mourning, and sacrifices. By his generosity, he won all. By his sincerity, he made the people repose trust in him. By his earnest activity, his achievements were great. By his justice, all were delighted.
Zizhang asked Confucius, saying, "What must a man be like that he may be employed in government?" The Master said, "He who honors the five excellent things and banishes the four bad things may be employed in government." Zizhang said, "What are meant by the five excellent things?" The Master said, "When the man in authority is beneficent without great expenditure; when he lays tasks on the people without their repining; when he pursues what he desires without being covetous; when he maintains a dignified ease without being proud; when he is majestic without being fierce." Zizhang said, "What is meant by being beneficent without great expenditure?" The Master replied, "When the man in authority makes more beneficial to the people the things from which they naturally derive benefit—is not this being beneficent without great expenditure? When he chooses the labors which are proper, and makes them labor on them, who will repine? When his desires are set on benevolent government, and he secures it, who will accuse him of covetousness? Whether he has to do with many people or few, or with things great or small, he does not dare to indicate any disrespect—is not this to maintain a dignified ease without any pride? He adjusts his clothes and cap, and throws a dignity into his looks, so that, thus dignified, he is looked at with awe—is not this to be majestic without being fierce?" Zizhang then asked, "What are meant by the four bad things?" The Master said, "To put the people to death without having instructed them—this is called cruelty. To require from them, suddenly, the full tale of work, without having given them warning—this is called oppression. To issue orders as if without urgency, at first, and, when the time comes, to insist on them with severity—this is called injury. And, generally, in the giving pay or rewards to men, to do it in a stingy way—this is called acting the part of a mere official."
Confucius said, "Without recognizing the ordinances of Heaven, it is impossible to be a superior man. Without an acquaintance with the rules of Propriety, it is impossible for the character to be established. Without knowing the force of words, it is impossible to know men."

zh:
洛神阁下：

昔年，为窃韦氏侠名，乃携“人面花”谒阁下，声泪俱下，诳语欺君……
当日所言“余生必正胜乐门楣”、“重立侠义之道”云云……皆为粉饰之辞。
……业果难逃，诸谎成谶。
今小舟知我当年伪造时疫、毒杀韦氏、殃及无辜……竟尽揽己身，决然长逝。
今亦从之，假手于人，自了残躯。唯求复本来面目，黄泉下，以真颜与吾妻相见。
匣中尺素，乃小舟初贻。
愿同葬来生岸，泉台共展。
en:
Honorable Water Lady:

Years ago, in order to steal the chivalrous name of the Wei Family, I brought the "Human-Faced Flower" to seek an audience with you. With tears in my eyes, I spoke lies to deceive you... All my vows that day about "rectifying the Shengle Sect's honor for the rest of my life" and "re-establishing the path of justice"... were nothing but hollow embellishments.
...One cannot escape the karma of their deeds, and all my lies have become a curses fulfilled.
Now, Xiaozhou has learned of my past sins: faking the plague, poisoning the Wei Family, and bringing ruin upon the innocent... She actually took all the guilt upon herself and resolutely chose death.
Today, I shall follow her. By borrowing the hands of another, I will end this broken life. My only plea is to restore my original appearance, so that in the underworld, I may face my beloved wife with my true face.
The silken letter in this box is the very first token Xiaozhou gave me.
I only wish for us to be buried together on the shores of the next life, unrolling this scroll together by the yellow springs.

function NpcTalkOptionsController:destroy_object()
	self:pop_mouse_visible()
	if self.model_options then
		self.model_options:destroy_object()
	end
	self:leave_camera()
	if self.target_id then
		local target_entity = G.space:get_entity(self.target_id)
		if target_entity then
			if target_entity.fake_server then
				target_entity.fake_server.dispatcher:dispatch(event_consts.E_TALK_CHOOSE_UI_CLOSE, dict())
			else
				target_entity:call_server_entity_method("rpc_send_event_to_npc_ai", "E_TALK_CHOOSE_UI_CLOSE", dict())
			end
			target_entity:try_pop_interact_flag(interact_component_consts.NPC_INTERACTING_FLAG_TALK_OPTIONS)
		end
	end

	G.mouse_manager:pop_show_mouse("talk_option")
	NpcTalkOptionsController.super.destroy_object(self)
end

function NpcTalkOptionsController:init(kwargs)
	kwargs = kwargs or dict()
	NpcTalkOptionsController.super.init(self, kwargs)
	self:on_enter()
	self.view.template_btn_info_2_view:set_visible(false)
	self.listview_options = self:create_child(TalkOptionsListViewController, self.view:get_node("listview_1"))
	self.target_id = kwargs:get("entity_id")
	if self.target_id then
		local target = G.space:get_entity(self.target_id)
		if target then
			target:try_push_interacting_flag(interact_component_consts.NPC_INTERACTING_FLAG_TALK_OPTIONS, true)
		end
	end
	local extra_data = kwargs:get("extra_data", dict())
	if kwargs:get("model_options") then
		self.model_options = kwargs:get("model_options")
	else
		self.model_options = NpcTalkOptionsModel(G.main_player_id, kwargs:get("entity_id"), extra_data)
	end
	self.listview_options:set_model(self.model_options)
	self:_add_dispatcher(G.gui_dispatcher, event_consts.E_LEAVE_INTERACT_AREA_TOTALLY, function(e, d) self:on_leave_interact_area(e, d) end)
	self:_add_dispatcher(G.gui_dispatcher, event_consts.E_DIALOG_NO_MOVE_UI_PLAY, function(e,d) self:on_reenter(e, d) end)
	self:init_sys_d()
	self:enter_camera()
	self:play_enter_dialog()
end

function NpcTalkOptionsController:on_enter()
	self.view:play_anim("vx_in")
	self:push_mouse_visible()
end

function NpcTalkOptionsController:on_reenter(event, data)
	self:on_enter()
end

function NpcTalkOptionsController:play_enter_dialog()
	self:pop_mouse_visible()
	local dialog_no = self.options_sys_d:get("dialog_id")
	if not bool(dialog_no) then
		dialog_no = G.datam.npc_talk_option_default_params[1]:get("default_xianhua")
	end

	if type(dialog_no) == "list" then
		local idx = math.random(#dialog_no)
		dialog_no = dialog_no[idx]
	end

	if G.space then
		G.space:start_dialogs(dialog_no, dict(
			target_id=self.target_id, stop_callback= function(finished) return self:on_enter_dialog_stop(finished) end
		))
	end
end

function NpcTalkOptionsController:on_enter_dialog_stop(finished)
	-- G.logger:info("lk", "==================== on_enter_dialog_stop: %s", finished)
	if self:is_destroyed() then
		return
	end

	if bool(self.model_options:get_only_exit_option()) then
		self.window:close() -- 需要立刻退出，因为正常退出有淡出动效
		--self.window:start_close()
		return
	end
	if #self.listview_options:get_items() <= 1 then
		-- 可能有其他选项，但是都被隐藏了，只有离开，那么也要立即退出
		self.window:close()
	end
	self:push_mouse_visible()
end

function NpcTalkOptionsWindow:on_reenter()
	self.controller:on_reenter()
end

世有不见山，隐烟霞之中。唯余一崖关，连墨门内外。崖关悬险，古来鲜有过崖关者。开运初，晋中有侠仇越海，试以轻功越之，力竭不迨。其慨然叹曰，“郁确其高，嗟吁叹也”。
常人若寻通关之法，需入崖关之内，经守崖人首肯。江湖传言，今之守崖人乃墨门三杰之一。其名为鹭，以眼力称道。初入江湖，即闻名诸牛耳。后不知何故，乃自守崖关，深居简出。逮乎今日，已有三年矣。
en:
Hidden Mountain lies veiled in mist and cloud. Only one route connects Mohist Hill to the outside world: a cliff pass known as Gasping Cliff. It is a hanging, perilous way, and since ancient times, few have ever made it across.
Early in the Kaiyun era, a wanderer from Jinzhong named Qiu Yuehai tried to clear it with lightness skill, but he ran out of strength and fell short. He could only gasp at its height and mutter a shaken sigh.
For ordinary travelers, the only way through is to enter the pass and win the guardian's approval. Jianghu whispers say the current guardian is one of Mohist Hill's Three Paragons, Heron, famed for her uncanny eyesight. She made a name for herself early on, then withdrew for reasons unknown and took up watch at Gasping Cliff. It has been three years now.

世皆传沧浪剑谱之玄，摘星手之奇，未谙狼山一战，吾辈境遇之哀。
昔吾等同门赴狼山，觅剑谱之秘。师妹凭其身法，夺得剑谱。然不日，契丹铁骑犯境，百姓流离，纷入狼山，求庇于吾辈。侠之大者，为国为民，吾等岂敢辞却？然山林多舛，继而大雪封径，粮尽援绝，契丹围之。如此十日十夜后，死伤枕藉。大师兄与小师弟奋勇杀敌，终殒于敌刃之下。而百姓身亡之际，竟以己之命，换吾等生路。战后，师妹渺无音讯，吾则遁入鬼市，疗治创伤。
此十余年间，吾惑愈甚。若单刀无以扛天下，为侠者，当何以处之？
en:
The world praises the mystery of the Canglang Sword Manual and the wonder of the Star Stealer, yet none know the sorrow of our plight in the Wolf Mountain Battle. 
Back then, my fellow disciples and I journeyed to Wolf Mountain in search of the manual's secrets. My younger martial sister, using her peerless agility, claimed the scroll. But soon after, Khitan cavalry invaded, displacing commoners who fled to Wolf Mountain for refuge. A true hero defends the nation and its people—how could we turn them away? Yet the mountains proved treacherous: heavy snow sealed the paths, supplies ran dry, and Khitans besieged us. After ten days and nights, the dead and wounded lay everywhere. My eldest martial brother and youngest disciple fought bravely, but fell by enemy blades. Strangely, as the commoners perished, they sacrificed themselves to buy us escape. After the battle, my sister vanished without a trace, and I fled to the Ghostlight Market to heal my wounds. 
For over a decade, my confusion has grown: if a single blade cannot bear the world's burdens, how should a hero act?

zh:
【士相见礼第三】

士相见之礼。挚，冬用雉，夏用腒。左头奉之，曰：“某也愿见，无由达。某子以命命某见。”主人对曰：“某子命某见，吾子有辱。请吾子之就家也，某将走见。”宾对曰：“某不足以辱命，请终赐见。”主人曰：“某不敢为仪，固请吾子之就家也，某将走见。”宾对曰：“某不敢为仪，固以请。”主人对曰：“某也固辞，不得命，将走见。闻吾子称挚，敢辞挚。”宾对曰：“某不以挚，不敢见。”主人对曰：“某不足以习礼，敢固辞。”宾对曰：“某也不依于挚，不敢见，固以请。”主人对曰：“某也固辞，不得命，敢不敬从！”出迎于门外，再拜。客答再拜。主人揖，入门右。宾奉挚，入门左。主人再拜受，宾再拜送挚，出。主人请见，宾反见，退。主人送于门外，再拜。
主人复见之，以其挚，曰：“曏者吾子辱，使某见。请还挚于将命者。”主人对曰：“某也既得见矣，敢辞。”宾对曰：“某也非敢求见，请还挚于将命者。”主人对曰：“某也既得见矣，敢固辞。”宾对曰：“某不敢以闻，固以请于将命者。”主人对曰：“某也固辞，不得命，敢不从？”宾奉挚入，主人再拜受。宾再拜送挚，出。主人送于门外，再拜。
士见于大夫，终辞其挚。于其入也，一拜其辱也。宾退，送，再拜。
若尝为臣者，则礼辞其挚，曰：“某也辞，不得命，不敢固辞。”宾入，奠挚，再拜，主人答壹拜，宾出。使摈者还其挚于门外，曰：“某也使其还挚。”宾对曰：“某也既得见矣，敢辞。”摈者对曰：“某也命某：‘某非敢为仪也。’敢以请。”宾对曰：“某也，夫子之贱私，不足以践礼，敢固辞！”摈者对曰：“某也使某，不敢为仪也，固以请！”宾对曰：“某固辞，不得命，敢不从？”再拜受。
下大夫相见以雁，饰之以布，维之以索，如执雉。上大夫相见以羔，饰之以布，四维之，结于面；左头，如麛执之。如士相见之礼。
……
en:
【The Third Ceremony: Scholar's Initial Meeting】

The ceremony of scholars meeting each other. For the introductory gift, in winter a pheasant is used, and in summer a dried pheasant. Holding it with the head to the left, the visitor says, "I have long wished to see you, but had no way to arrange it. So-and-so, on your behalf, instructed me to come and meet you." The host replies, "So-and-so instructed me to meet you, and you have condescended to come. I beg that you would return to your home, and I will hasten to call on you." The guest replies, "I am not worthy of such condescension; I beg that you would finally grant me an audience." The host says, "I would not presume to stand on ceremony; I earnestly beg that you would return to your home, and I will hasten to call on you." The guest replies, "I would not presume to stand on ceremony; I earnestly make this request." The host replies, "I have earnestly declined, but cannot refuse your command; I will hasten to meet you. I hear that you bring an introductory gift; I venture to decline the gift." The guest replies, "Without my gift, I would not dare to see you." The host replies, "I am not worthy to practice such rites; I venture to decline firmly." The guest replies, "Without relying on my gift, I would not dare to see you; I earnestly make this request." The host replies, "I have earnestly declined, but cannot refuse your command; I dare not but respectfully comply!" He goes out to welcome him outside the gate, and bows twice. The guest returns the bows twice. The host makes a bow, and enters by the right side of the gate. The guest, holding the gift, enters by the left side. The host bows twice and receives it; the guest bows twice and presents the gift, then exits. The host requests an audience, and the guest returns for a visit, then withdraws. The host escorts him outside the gate and bows twice.
The host then returns the visit, using the same gift, saying, "Previously you condescended to come, causing me to meet you. I beg to return this gift to your messenger." The host (now the guest) replies, "I have already had the honor of meeting you; I venture to decline." The guest (now the host) replies, "I do not presume to seek an audience; I beg to return the gift to your messenger." The host replies, "I have already had the honor of meeting you; I venture to decline firmly." The guest replies, "I would not dare to make this known to you, but I earnestly request it through your messenger." The host replies, "I have earnestly declined, but cannot refuse your command; dare I not comply?" The guest, holding the gift, enters; the host bows twice and receives it. The guest bows twice and presents the gift, then exits. The host escorts him outside the gate and bows twice.
When a scholar meets a high official, the latter finally declines the gift. Upon his entering, he bows once to acknowledge the condescension. When the guest withdraws, he escorts him out and bows twice.
If the visitor had formerly been a retainer, then the gift is declined with courtesy, saying, "I decline it, but cannot refuse your command; I dare not decline firmly." The guest enters, places the gift down, and bows twice; the host returns one bow, and the guest exits. He sends a messenger to return the gift outside the gate, saying, "So-and-so has sent me to return this gift." The guest replies, "I have already had the honor of meeting him; I venture to decline." The messenger replies, "So-and-so instructed me, saying: 'I would not presume to stand on ceremony.' I venture to make this request." The guest replies, "I am but a humble servant of your master, not worthy to tread the path of ceremony; I venture to decline firmly!" The messenger replies, "So-and-so sent me, and would not presume to stand on ceremony; I earnestly make this request!" The guest replies, "I have earnestly declined, but cannot refuse your command; dare I not comply?" He bows twice and receives it.
When lower-ranking officials meet, they use a wild goose as the gift, adorned with cloth and tied with cords, held in the same manner as a pheasant. When higher-ranking officials meet, they use a lamb as the gift, adorned with cloth, bound with four cords, and tied at the head; holding the head to the left, as one holds a fawn. This follows the same ceremony as that of scholars meeting.

他似人似鬼，似正似邪。有时他是最慈悲的公子，吟诵佛经，为那些被世道所害的无辜女子送行。有时他又是最可怕的凶煞，轻晃纸伞，将那些挡在面前的人尽数斩杀。

en:
Among the Fourteen Fiends of Ghost Street, none inspire more fear than the Seventh—Ghost Master Jiang Kui. 
Man or ghost? Virtue or vice? No one knows for sure. At times, he is the gentlest of princes, reciting sutras and bidding farewell to innocent women crushed by a cruel world. Other times, he becomes a nightmare cloaked in flesh, spinning his paper umbrella as he cuts down all who stand before him. 
They respect him. They fear him. But none understand him. 
And Jiang Kui doesn't care. For years, he has wandered in a faded wedding robe, waiting for one who will never return. Day and night blur into a haze of remorse that gnaws through the soul. And when he heard rumors of a remedy hidden deep in the Mistveil Forest, a drug that could raise the dead, restore flesh to bone. For the first time in years, he felt truly awake. 
Sis... even if it's a fool's errand, A'kui must take this path.

九四六年的那天，刘娴回到这挂着“张家食肆“的屋子时，屋里还亮着灯，她摸了摸手臂上的疤，那块皮皱巴巴地缩在一起。
那是他爹赌输了钱，喝醉了酒回来，将灯摔在她身上弄的。
从第一个疤起，她在外头做工回家后，见到家里的灯没灭，就知道爹定是喝多了酒，倒头便躺了。
她本就瘦，将自己皱巴巴缩成一团走进门，像极了那一道被烫伤的疤。
她得把步子放轻一点，再轻一点，轻到和她在这个世上的重量一样——可有可无、无关紧要。
她提防着惊醒她爹，又害怕她爹，便不敢往那看，只畏畏缩缩地走，死死地盯着那盏灯，灯火微微晃荡一下，她像是被烫了一下，绷紧，猛然顿住，直到悄无声息再迈步，直到将自个塞在一个离灯最远的角落，祈祷天快亮，祈祷天亮了他也不醒。
她不和她娘一样，她娘在身上只有五道疤的时候就跑了，她跑不了。
一个只有七岁的女娃娃，门内门外，这世道对她来说，都是一盏烫得吓人的灯。
她还在想着，在外头徘徊的脚步像是被人听见了，那个昨日见过的，叫做张安康的人挑着灯走到门口，她藏起自己从外头偷来的吃食，向后退了一步。
“咋不进来。“
他瞧起来像个好人，但像个好人的人太多了，多到里面也放得下太多坏人。
熟悉的桌上、熟悉的灯下，一碗热气腾腾的面。
她目光茫然：“这是什么？”
因为她的话语。他脸上的茫然也如此明显：“面，但只有一碗了，咱分着吃成不？”
对他来说送人饭吃，等人吃饭，就像是对她来说的世道杀人，人杀人一样理所当然。
刘娴想，在这场战争之前，他一定过得很好，以至于还是一个好人。
en:
On that day in 946, when Liu Xian returned to the house with the sign "Zhang's Eatery" over the door, the lights were still on inside. She touched the scar on her arm. The skin there was wrinkled and puckered.
Her father had lost money gambling, come home drunk, and smashed a lamp on her. That's how she got the scar.
From the very first scar, she learned: if she came home from her odd jobs and saw the lamp still burning, it meant her father had been drinking and had already collapsed somewhere inside.
She was already skinny, and she'd scrunch herself up as small as possible when she walked in, looking as shriveled and fragile as the burn on her arm.
She would step as lightly as she could, lighter and lighter, until her footsteps were as weightless as her whole existence: barely there, easily overlooked.
She was always on guard, careful not to wake her father, and too scared to even look his way. So she would creep through the house, eyes locked on that lamp. If the flame so much as flickered, she'd freeze, bracing herself as if she'd been burned, not daring to move again until everything was completely silent. Then, she'd inch herself into the farthest, darkest corner from the lamp, praying for dawn, praying that when morning came, he still wouldn't wake.
She wasn't like her mother. Her mother had run away when she had only five scars; Liu Xian couldn't run.
She was just a seven-year-old girl. Inside the house or out, the world felt like a burning lamp she was terrified to touch.
She was still thinking about all this, pacing outside, when her footsteps must have caught someone's attention. The man she'd seen the day before, Zhang Ankang, came to the door with a lantern. She quickly hid the food she'd stolen and took a step back.
"Why don't you come inside?"
He looked like a good man, but she'd learned there were plenty of people who looked good, enough to make room for plenty of bad ones, too.
Inside, at the same old table under the same old lamp, was a bowl of steaming noodles.
She stared at it blankly. "What is this?"
Her confusion was reflected on his face. "Noodles, but there's just one bowl left. How about we share?"
For him, offering food to someone or waiting for someone to eat seemed as natural as breathing. For her, in this world, it felt as impossible as killing or being killed.
Liu Xian thought that, before this war, he must have lived a good life, to still be able to be a good person.

Shi Xiao Lu Ya

zh:
自上回见识过张万师的水转百戏，你便对他的剑姬人偶念念不忘。
于是，你再度潜入水下，登门拜访。张万师依然昏昏沉沉，醉卧在地。只是与上回不同，在他的面前，多出了两个斟满的酒杯。
他在等谁共饮？又在期待些什么？思考许久，你决定拿出……
#Y【飞天城图纸……】你并未有此物，只是想试探张万师的反应。#E
静静地将图纸放在了他的身边。张万师似醉似醒，似是捕捉到了封页上的字眼。他用手轻轻一勾，拿起整摞图纸，看了两眼，又丢到了一旁。他拍了拍手，桃靥剑姬优雅地将你请离了墨守之心。
“此路无知己，明珠莫暗投……你且去吧。”

今夜，他依然与明月对饮。
en:
Ever since witnessing Zhang Wanshi's Aquatic Spectacle, you have been haunted by the memory of his Swordsworn automaton.
Thus, you dive beneath the waves once more to pay him a visit. Zhang Wanshi remains in a stupor, lying drunk upon the ground. Yet, unlike before, two brimful wine cups now rest in front of him.
Who is he waiting to drink with? What is he longing for? After much thought, you decide to present...
#Y[The Skyward City diagrams...] You do not actually have the diagrams. You only wish to gauge Zhang Wanshi's reaction.#E
You quietly place the diagrams by his side. Half-drunk and half-awake, Zhang Wanshi seems to catch a glimpse of the words upon the cover. With a casual flick of his finger, he lifts the stack of diagrams, spares them a glance, and casts them aside. He claps his hands, and the Rosy-Faced Swordsworn elegantly ushers you out from the Changeless Heart.
"There's no one here who truly understands you. Don't let your gifts go to waste... You should move on."

Tonight, he drinks with the bright moon once more.
Yu Bu

zh:
【昭公第十】

元年，春，王正月，公即位。
〇叔孙豹会晋赵武、楚公子围、齐国酌、宋向戍、卫石恶、陈公子招、蔡公孙归生、郑轩虎、许人、曹人于漷。
此陈侯之弟招也，何以不称弟？贬。曷为贬？为杀世子偃师贬，曰陈侯之弟招杀陈世子偃师。大夫相杀称人，此其称名氏以杀何？言将自是弑君也。今将尔，词曷为与亲弑者同？君亲无将，将而必诛焉。然则曷为不于其弑焉贬？以亲者弑，然后其罪恶甚。春秋不待贬绝而罪恶见者，不贬绝以见罪恶也。贬绝然后罪恶见者，贬绝以见罪恶也。今招之罪已重矣，曷为复贬乎此？著招之有罪也。何著乎招之有罪？言楚之托乎讨招以灭陈也。
〇三月，取运。
运者何？内之邑也。其言取之何？不听也。
〇夏，秦伯之弟针出奔晋。
秦无大夫，此何以书？仕诸晋也。曷为仕诸晋？有千乘之国，而不能容其母弟，故君子谓之出奔也。
〇六月，丁巳，邾娄子华卒。
〇晋荀吴帅师，败狄于大原。
此大卤也，曷为谓之大原？地物从中国，邑人名从主人。原者何？上平曰原，下平曰隰。
〇秋，莒去疾自齐入于莒。
〇莒展出奔吴。
〇叔弓帅师疆运田。
疆运田者何？与莒为竟也。与莒为竟，则曷为帅师而往？畏莒也。葬邾娄悼公。
〇冬，十有一月，己酉，楚子卷卒。
〇楚公子比出奔晋。

二年，春，晋侯使韩起来聘。
〇夏，叔弓如晋。
〇秋，郑杀其大夫公孙黑。
〇冬，公如晋，至河乃复。
其言至河乃复何？不敢进也。
〇季孙宿如晋。

……
en:
【Duke Zhao, Year 10】

Year 1, Spring, the King's first month, the Duke assumed the throne.
〇Shusun Bao met with Jin's Zhao Wu, Chu's Prince Wei, Qi's Guo Zhuo, Song's Xiang Xu, Wei's Shi E, Chen's Prince Zhao, Cai's Gongsun Guisheng, Zheng's Xuan Hu, Xu's envoy, and Cao's envoy at Guo.
This is Chen's Prince Zhao, the Duke's younger brother. Why is he not called "younger brother"? Because he was demoted. Why was he demoted? He was demoted for killing the heir apparent, Shi Shi, and it is said, "Chen's Prince Zhao, the Duke's younger brother, killed Chen's heir apparent, Shi Shi." When high officials kill each other, they are referred to by their rank, but why is he referred to by name and clan here for the killing? It is to say that from this point, he would go on to kill his ruler. Now, since he intended to do so, why is his wording the same as one who actually killed his ruler? For a ruler and his kin, there is no room for intent; if there is intent, execution is mandatory. Then why was he not demoted at the time of the killing? Because when a close relative commits the killing, then his crime is even more severe. In the Spring and Autumn Annals, when a crime is evident without demotion or severance, it is not demoted or severed to reveal the crime. When a crime becomes evident only after demotion and severance, it is demoted and severed to reveal the crime. Now Zhao's crime is already grave; why is he demoted again here? To make clear that Zhao has guilt. What is made clear about Zhao's guilt? It is to say that Chu used the pretext of punishing Zhao to extinguish Chen.
〇In the third month, Yun was taken.
What is Yun? It is an internal city. Why is it said to be "taken"? Because it did not obey.
〇In Summer, Qin's Duke's younger brother, Zhen, fled to Jin.
Qin had no high officials; why is this recorded? Because he took office in Jin. Why did he take office in Jin? Having a state of a thousand chariots, yet unable to accommodate his own younger brother, thus the gentleman calls it "fleeing."
〇In the sixth month, on Ding Si, Zhu Lou's Zi Hua died.
〇Jin's Xun Wu led troops and defeated the Di at Taiyuan.
This is Dalu, why is it called Taiyuan? The names of places and things follow the Central States, while the names of towns and people follow their masters. What is "yuan"? High and flat is called "yuan," low and flat is called "xi."
〇In Autumn, Ju's Quji entered Ju from Qi.
〇Ju Zhan fled to Wu.
〇Shu Gong led troops to demarcate the fields of Yun.
What does "demarcating the fields of Yun" mean? It is to establish the boundary with Ju. If establishing the boundary with Ju, then why lead troops there? Because they feared Ju. Buried Zhu Lou's Duke Dao.
〇In Winter, in the eleventh month, on Ji You, Chu's Zi Juan died.
〇Chu's Prince Bi fled to Jin.

Year 2, Spring, Jin's Marquis sent Han Qi on a diplomatic visit.
〇In Summer, Shu Gong went to Jin.
〇In Autumn, Zheng killed its high official, Gongsun Hei.
〇In Winter, the Duke went to Jin, reaching the Yellow River, then returned.
What does it mean that he reached the Yellow River and then returned? He did not dare to advance.
〇Ji Sun Su went to Jin.

……
Youngster, don't take another step forward!

当康陶穿行土丘之间，匠以其观土壤之变。其遇土中异物则食，亦常收集许多未得料想之物。

The potter fashions the Bountiful Pig to store all grains, that the world's granaries may brim and the people have plenty.

Zhejiang Crossing lies beyond Houchao Gate, once known as the ancient Willow Shore. Qiantang boasts many ferries, of which Willow Shore on the northern bank and Xixing on the southern bank are most renowned; its river winds and turns, its tides rising ten thousand fathoms high, and so it is also called Zhejiang, the Winding River.

The Wuyue Region enjoys the boon of its waterways, with roads open in every direction, and even common folk's boats may venture out to sea. Thus, at today's Zhejiang Crossing, boats and oars gather in such multitude that one cannot see where they begin or end.

Vessels converge here from every direction—southern goods and northern treasures, eastern delicacies and western grain, all gathered without exception. The rarities of all corners of the realm find their way here—why then seek them from afar?

zh:
活人医馆不开张，天不收乐得清闲，躺在小榻上心算这个月又赚进多少黄金。忽然有人抽走了他盖在脸上的记账本。天不收正要发作，却发现来的人是寒香寻。他只好躺下背过身去，嘴里还念叨着：“不开张不开张，今天我要睡觉。”

“快起来，给我做瓶千金尽。”寒香寻开口便是一瓶千金尽，送上门的钱哪有不赚的道理？天不收一个翻身就从床上起身，正打算谢谢眼前这尊财神，转念一想却品出不对。神仙渡里能有什么大灾大病？寒香寻这人又抠搜的很，会一次要这么多千金尽大概又是为了那个人。想到这儿天不收歇了打趣的心思，慢吞吞地挪到桌前开始制药。手里没闲着，心里想着，嘴上便问了出来：“又是为了那位褚大侠？”

“哼，那傻子非要去送死，备点药免得他到时候真死了还得我收拾。”
天不收撇撇嘴，小声嘀咕了句：“他傻？你难道不傻？"

寒香寻瞪了他一眼。

“我也是个傻的。只有傻子才会大好的时光不睡觉，爬起来给你的情人做伤药！”天不收撇了撇嘴，幽幽地说。

寒香寻别过脸去，没再说话。活人医馆里只剩下天不收捣药的声音。
en:
Evercare Clinic is quiet, and Unfated Tian enjoys the rare peace. He lies sprawled on a narrow bed, putting the ledger over his face and mentally calculates how much money he's made this month. Suddenly, the ledger is abruptly snatched. He sits up, annoyed. "Hey..." Then he sees who it is: Han Xiangxun. He turns his back to her and mumbles, "No patients today. I'm going back to sleep."

"Get up. I need a bottle of Priceless Antidote." Her tone is chipper, and his eyes light up. Business is business, and gold is gold. He flips over with renewed energy, already shaping a smile to thank his generous patron. But then a thought strikes him. There has never been any serious illness at Heaven's Pier that would call for this medicine. And she, stingy as ever, wouldn't be here unless it were for someone else. It has to be for him. Realizing that, the doctor drops his usual teasing. He turns to his desk and begins preparing the medicine in silence. Still, curiosity gets the better of him. As he grinds the herbs, he asks, "Is this for that swordsman again? That Hero Chu?"

"That fool throws himself into danger without a second thought. I'm just preparing this in case he winds up half-dead again. Someone's got to clean up his mess."
Unfated Tian clicks his tongue and mutters, "Fool? Who's really the fool here?"

Han Xiangxun shoots him a sharp look.

"Alright, alright. I'm the fool. Only a fool would drag himself out of bed at such a good time to make medicine for someone else's 'fool'." He pouts, voice soft and petulant.

Han Xiangxun turns away, saying nothing more. Silence settles over the clinic once again, broken only by the steady rhythm of herbs being ground beneath stone.

zh:
一更了。今夜敲梆子的是老孙头，我听得出来。
他的梆子声比旁人轻，轻里带着颤——从前不是这样的。从前他总把梆子敲得又重又脆，但那天之后，他便再也敲不出那样的声了。
梆子一下，两下……孙老头走得很慢，但还是越走越远了。也只有他，从不往这殿的窗格里瞧。他的眼睛空茫茫的，像蒙着秋雾的井。
我也是。
我们都在那场雨里湿透过。

那是乾佑元年的秋。那天的雨，真大啊，砸在殿瓦上，像是老天爷也在捶鼓鸣冤。
可殿内静得骇人。
乌泱泱的官老爷们立在那里，像一片黑压压的树林。他们的眼长在头顶，心藏在脚下。
他们都知道李大人为何而死。
他因忠直而死，因知恩而死，因党祸而死。
但圣意已然劈下，那么他的死就得换个缘由。
——“谋危社稷，潜结奸凶，拟为叛乱。”
这字字句句，将他砸进了烂泥里。谁也没再说什么，谁也说不得什么。
风雨要竹子弯，它便只能折。满殿的人看着它折，看着它碎，看着它被泥水卷走。然后他们沉默转身，各自撑开了伞。
我也有一把伞。我死死攥着它，指甲嵌进伞柄里。可我最终，没有往前迈那一步。
于是李大人的叹息，就那么融进了这皇宫的上空。与每次大典乐声的消散那般，无甚差别。

漫天的雨水落下来，一滴，又一滴，敲在砖上，声音比此刻老孙头的梆子还清楚。
我没有错。一个小内侍，连头顶的半寸天都撑不起，更何论去辩一场已定的局？
两年了，我每晚都这么对自己嘀咕，像念一道保命的符。可这道符镇不住梦——梦里下着好大的雨，从不停歇。
上个月，和老孙头吃酒。酒冷了，他忽然没头没尾地说：“李大人……从前最爱笑我的梆子声。” 说完他就笑了，笑得比哭还难听。
从前他总说，人活一世，要对得起祖宗牌位。如今他只说，酒冷了，得热一热。
我们都学会了喝冷酒，说热话。

那一滴，一滴的雨，就这样渗了好些年。从殿外的砖缝，渗到了这殿的地上，渗进了我的骨头里。
而我还在写。
这些字，会被虫蛀，被灰埋，或许永远等不到被看见的一天。
那我写什么呢？写给自己听吗？写给后人看吗？
我不知道。
我只觉得冷，月色照亮了我脚下的砖地，却照不到我。
在这个夜晚，在过去的很多个夜晚，在之后的更多个夜晚……都照不到我。
en:
The first watch has begun. Old Sun is on the clapper tonight. I can tell.
His clapper sounds lighter than other men's, light and faintly trembling. It was not always so. In years past he struck it hard and sharp, but after that day it was never the same again.
One strike, then another. Old Sun walks slowly, but the sound still drifts farther and farther away. He alone never looks toward the lattice windows of this hall. His eyes are empty, like a well veiled in autumn mist.
So are mine.
We were both soaked through in that rain.

It was in the autumn of 948. The rain that day was fierce, hammering on the palace tiles as though Heaven itself were beating a drum to cry out against injustice.
And yet inside the hall, the silence was more terrible still.
The officials stood there in a dark mass, like a stand of black trees. Their eyes sat high above, their hearts buried below.
They all knew why Lord Li had died.
He died for loyalty. He died for gratitude. He died in the ruin of factional strife.
But once the imperial will had fallen, his death had to be given another name.
"He endangered the altars of state, consorted in secret with traitors and villains, and plotted rebellion."
Word by word, they pressed him down into the mud. No one spoke again. No one could.
When wind and rain demand that bamboo bend, then bend it must, until at last it breaks. The whole hall watched it bend, watched it split, watched it be swept away in the mire. Then they turned in silence, and each raised his own umbrella.
I had an umbrella too. I gripped it so hard my nails bit into the handle.
But in the end, I did not step forward.
And so Lord Li's sigh dissolved into the sky above the palace, no different from the way the music of a grand ceremony rises and fades.

The rain kept falling, drop after drop, striking the bricks more clearly than even Old Sun's clapper now.
I was not wrong. I was only a young palace attendant. I could not even hold up the half inch of sky above my own head, much less contend with a judgment already sealed.
For two years now, I have whispered this to myself every night, like a charm to keep myself alive.
But no charm can quiet a dream. In the dream, the rain falls hard and never stops.
Last month I drank with Old Sun. The wine had gone cold when he suddenly said, "Lord Li... used to laugh most at the sound of my clapper." Then he laughed too, and the sound of it was uglier than weeping.
He used to say a man should live so that he could face his ancestors' tablets without shame. Now he says only that the wine has gone cold and ought to be warmed.
We have both learned to drink cold wine and speak warm words.

Drop by drop, that rain has gone on seeping through the years. From the cracks in the bricks outside the hall, onto the floor within, and into my very bones.
And still I write.
These words will be eaten by insects, buried in dust, perhaps never seen by anyone at all.
Then why do I write? To let myself hear them. To leave them for those who come after.
I do not know.
I know only that I am cold. Moonlight falls on the bricks at my feet, but it does not reach me.
Not on this night. Not on all the nights already gone. Not on all the nights still to come.

喜气洋洋过了三日，少东家收拾好了玩具零嘴准备出门。还没走到渡口，就见寒香寻与江无浪等在路上。少东家当然不服气，嚷着江无浪明明已经同意自己去闯荡江湖，怎么还不讲武德叫来寒姨逮人？江无浪说自己只说能去，可以去，眼下少东家轻易就被寒香寻抓到，自然说明是不能去了。少东家还没来得及反驳就被寒香寻提走。小船撑开一片涟漪，江无浪在船上回望那一大一小两个身影，渐行渐远。
en:
At Blissful Retreat, Jiang Wulang drank alone, as he often did, savoring the silence that came with moonlight. Word of his impending departure had somehow reached the Young Master, who rushed over, begging to be taken along on his journey beyond Heaven's Pier. Jiang Wulang took a slow sip of wine and replied offhandedly, "If you can go, then go yourself." Overjoyed, the Young Master spent the next three days strutting around, telling everyone he met that a new hero was about to rise in the jianghu. The tale, of course, eventually made its way to Han Xiangxun.

When the day came, the Young Master brought snacks and toys and set off with great fanfare. Only to spot Han Xiangxun and Jiang Wulang waiting at the ferry. Outraged, the Young Master shouted that Jiang Wulang had already given permission to enter the jianghu, and he demanded to know why Han Xiangxun was here, too. Jiang Wulang answered calmly, "I said you can go, if you have the ability. But if Han Xiangxun catches you this easily, then clearly, you can't." Before the Young Master could fire back, Han Xiangxun had already grabbed his collar and hauled the would-be hero away. The small boat soon pushed off from the shore, ripples fanning out across the water. Jiang Wulang stood watching as the two figures grew smaller until they faded into the distance.

阴风吹黄蒿，挽歌渡秋水。车马却归城，孤坟月明里。
双辙出郭门，绵绵东西道。送死多于生，几人得终老。
见人切肺肝，不如归山好。不闻哀哭声，默默安怀抱。
时尽从物化，又免生忧扰。世间寿者稀，尽为悲伤恼。
en:
Gusty winds of gloom sweep yellow wormwood,
Dirges float across the autumn stream.
Carriages turn back to the walled city,
While a lone grave lies in moonlit beam. 
Twin wheel-tracks stretch beyond the city wall,
The east-west road winds on without end.
More funerals than births mark the days,
How many live to see their hoary age? 
To see men tear each other's hearts apart,
Better to retreat to the mountain's art.
Far from the wails of sorrow's refrain,
In silence, let my heart find its refrain. 
When time ends, let nature take its toll,
Thus freed from sorrow's endless scroll.
In this world, few live to ripe old age,
All are bound by grief's relentless cage.

zh:
泰山之巅，水陆十八道高手皆聚于此，却俱是满面乌云。只因这一年之中，武林已遭两大惊天祸事。
其一，乃年初之时，武林盟主宇文岳一家老小，与其庄中护卫上下一百余口，一夜之间尽数被戮，无一活口。
其二，乃不久之前，天河高家家主高群被一忽然现身的白发妖人一掌穿心，当场身陨。那白发妖人疯疯癫癫，却有一身诡异武功。高家剩余高手将其团团围住，仍奈何他不得，被他以浑厚掌力破围而出，不知所踪。
两庄惨案，皆有江湖名宿惨死，一时间江湖人人自危。若两桩惨案，皆是那白发妖人所为，真真可称魔头！
陆缘乃一云游四方的墨家门徒，站在那一群高手之间，轻轻敲了敲自己一路背来的机关巨匣。
“那魔头，不会是你吧？”
匣子里头，正是陆缘前些时日救下的一昏迷白发病人。因其白发招摇，故藏于匣中。
初时匣中无声，待高手们又谈论许久之后，病人却忽然逼音成线，传于陆缘耳中。
“你先行离开，我有要杀之人。”
陆缘大吃一惊，自己竟真救下那魔头。正欲劝阻，魔头已破匣而出。只见他抓向人群中一人，只一爪，便了断了那人性命！
山巅高手群聚而起，围攻向那魔头，竟一时拿之不下！
“那墨家子弟与其同行，定然有鬼，先拿她一问！”
本已杀出重围的白发魔头听闻此言，竟重返杀阵，将陆缘护住，拼出一身伤口，杀出重围。
是夜，至一破落庙宇。陆缘怒斥那白发魔头，怎可滥杀无辜。谁知白日所向无敌的魔头，闻言竟只落泪不语。见魔头身上皆是为救自己所留之上，陆缘心下不忍，只好问其缘由。
“我说了，你便信吗？”
白发魔头自知如今自己形貌与常人有异，只觉那陆缘未必肯信。

谁知那陆缘正是天真良善之徒，只让那魔头且说来一听。
“我本是盟主宇文岳之子，宇文天音。家母寿诞之际，竟有恶徒重金收买备宴之人，于酒宴之中下毒。待我醒来，家父正为护我，死于我眼前。我穿行烈火，方逃出重围。只是吸入火瘴之毒，须发尽白。那天河高家，假借救援之名，搜罗我家财富，更是将昏迷的我囚禁于高家地牢，日夜折磨，以求我家传排云掌之密。火瘴之毒虽改我形貌，亦拓我经脉，功力渐渐恢复之后，我挣脱枷锁，借机杀了那高家家主，如此才逃离出来。后又因负伤昏迷，为你所救。”
陆缘见他面善，讲述之时情真意切，又无不合逻辑之处，已信了五分。又因白日天音肯舍身救其性命，如此知恩图报，重情重义之辈，令她又信了五分。于是便助其分析：
“恰是盟主新换之际，何人最有望得盟主之位，说不得便是你之仇人。”
却说那盟主比武，经半月之较量，只剩五人有资格可夺那高位。
正比武之间，白发魔头忽然现世，众人竟尽皆惊惧，不敢与之匹敌。江湖众人皆面面相觑，那台上五人终是不肯如此颜面扫地，轮番出手。已五敌一，竟仍不是对手。
“此白发魔头，掌力为何如此雄浑！”
说时迟那时快，五人之中一人终于按捺不住，寻出宇文天音排云掌之破绽，突然出手，一剑破其命门。
正待欢欣，定睛一看，原来场中只是一偃偶。隐藏在暗处的宇文天音趁机杀出，一式排云掌，取了那恶徒性命。
江湖之人不明真相，围攻而来。那四名高手终于认出排云掌，不顾陆缘解释，向宇文天音杀去。
“宇文家不灭，武林各家永无翻身之地！”
宇文天音如梦初醒，原来，灭宇文全族上下，非一人之力。众多想染指盟主位的名门高派，或默许，或出力，共谋此事。当日，宇文天音化身杀神，以一人之力，斩杀无数高手，后携陆缘逃出阵去。
此后，江湖只见陆缘而不见宇文天音，却无一人敢对陆缘出手。传说那天下最可怖的魔头，就藏在她四处搬运的那机关匣中。陆缘参与次年之盟主大会，所有对手皆于前一日或降或匿，一路不交一战成为武林共主。她于盟主之位，澄清所谓白发魔头之恶名，次年便卸任归隐。后世人皆不知陆缘与宇文天音之下落。
en:
At the summit of Mount Tai, eighteen masters from across the jianghu have gathered, their brows all knit in a grim gloom, for within this single year, the jianghu has been rocked by two brutal calamities.
First was the massacre at the home of the Martial Alliance leader, Yuwen Yue. His entire kin, along with over a hundred estate guards, were slaughtered overnight. Not a single soul was left alive.
The second came not long ago, when Gao Qun, head of the Gao family of Tianhe, was struck through the heart and killed on the spot by a white-haired madman. The madman seemed utterly deranged, yet possessed a bizarre and fearsome martial art. Though the remaining Gao warriors surrounded him on all sides, they still could not stop him. He broke through with overwhelming palm force and vanished without a trace.
With renowned luminaries falling in both slaughters, a shadow of dread has fallen over the jianghu; every warrior now fears for their own life. Should both atrocities be the handiwork of that white-haired madman, he is nothing less than a demon incarnate!
Lu Yuan, a wandering disciple of the Mohist, stands amidst the giants. She gives a soft, rhythmic tap to the massive mechanical case strapped to her back:
"That demon... wouldn't be you, would it?"
Hidden within that case is the unconscious, white-haired patient she pulled from the brink of death days ago. His snow-white hair is too conspicuous, forcing her to conceal him within the case...
At first, the casket remained silent. But after the others whispered for some time, the patient suddenly channeled his voice into a focused thread of sound, vibrating directly into Lu Yuan's ear:
"Leave now. There is a life I must take."
Lu Yuan is stunned. She has actually rescued the very demon. Before she can utter a word of protest, the demon erupts from the case. With a predatory lunge, his fingers curve into a claw, snaring a man from the crowd. A single strike, and the life is snuffed out.
The masters spring to their feet and launch their attack, yet none can bring him down!
"That Mohist girl is his accomplice! There's foul play here. Seize her for questioning!"
Hearing that, the white-haired demon, who has already broken through the siege, plunges back into the lethal fray to shield Lu Yuan. Drenched in fresh blood and braving a rain of blades, he carves a path through the encirclement once more.
By nightfall, they find sanctuary within the crumbling walls of a derelict temple. Lu Yuan lashes out at the white-haired fiend, demanding how he could spill the blood of the innocent so ruthlessly. To her surprise, the man who seemed invincible in the daylight now only weeps in a heavy, hollow silence. Seeing the injuries he's suffered while protecting her, Lu softens and presses him for an explanation.
"If I were to speak the truth... would you even have the heart to believe me?"
The demon is well aware that his unusual appearance makes it hard for others to trust him.

But Lu Yuan, kind-hearted and innocent, is already all ears.
"I am Yuwen Tianyin, son of Chief Yuwen Yue. On my mother's birthday, vipers bribed our servants to poison the feast. I awoke to see my father fall, shielding me with his dying breath. I fled through an inferno, and the toxic miasma turned my hair white. The Gao Clan played the savior only to plunder our halls. They cast me into a lightless dungeon, torturing me for the secrets of our Cloud-Steering Palm. That poison altered my appearance, but it also broadened my meridians. As my strength gradually returned, I broke free of my shackles, seized the chance to kill Patriarch Gao, and escaped. Later, when I was wounded and unconscious once more, you saved me."
Lu Yuan studies his face. His words are raw with grief, the logic untainted by deceit. Her doubt softens; she believes him, at least in half. Since Tianyin has risked everything to save her, the remaining half of her heart follows suit. So she helps him piece things together:
"The timing is precise. The succession of the Alliance was at hand. He who covets the high seat most is likely the one with your father's blood on his hands."
After a fortnight of grueling trials, only five champions remain to vie for the supreme mantle.
Suddenly, the white-haired demon comes out of nowhere, and the crowd falls silent with fear. No one dares to face him. The five men exchange uneasy glances, unwilling to show weakness, and take turns launching their attacks against him. Even five against one, they can't overwhelm him.
"How did this white-haired demon get such overwhelming palm power?"
Just as one of them can no longer hold back, he spots a flaw in Yuwen Tianyin's Cloud-Steering Palm and lunges, driving his sword toward a vital spot.
But as the victor's cry dies in his throat, the truth is bared: the figure on the stage is nothing but a puppet. From the shroud of shadows, the real Yuwen Tianyin erupts. With a devastating strike of the Cloud-Steering Palm, he claims the villain's life.
The crowd, blinded by ignorance and fueled by rumors, surges forward in a frenzied assault. As the signature Cloud-Steering Palm is revealed, the four remaining warriors lunge at Yuwen Tianyin with lethal intent, despite Lu Yuan's cries.
"With the Yuwen line around in the jianghu, the rest of us will forever remain in their shadow!"
A chilling realization strikes Yuwen Tianyin: the annihilation of his kin was no solitary crime. The great sects, hungry for the supreme mantle, had woven a web of complicity, some through silent consent, others through active bloodletting. That day, through a storm of steel and blood, he carved a path for Lu Yuan and escaped the mountain's peak.
In the years that followed, Lu Yuan wandered in the jianghu alone. Yuwen Tianyin had vanished, yet no one dared to lay a finger on Lu Yuan. Whispers spread like wildfire: the world's most terrifying demon was slumbering within the case she bore upon her back. At the following year's Grand Assembly, Lu Yuan's rivals fled or surrendered before the first drumbeat. Without drawing a single blade, she ascended as the Sovereign of the Martial World. From her high seat, she washed away the infamy of the "White-Haired Demon." Her task complete, she abdicated her power and vanished into the mist. Their final destination remains a mystery, their names lost to the shifting winds of history.
